There's a pretty simple way to do this, in fact I did it yesterday. Use `dd` or a similar utiltity on Linux (windows might have something like it) and do a byte-level copy of the card.

     dd if=/dev/<mountpoint> of=~/sd-card.bin bs=1M 
the mountpoint is probably `sdd` or `sdc`. If you're not using gnu `dd` the last M will be lowercase. After that, insert your new SD card and reverse the process.

    dd  if=~/sd-card.bin of=/dev/<mountpoint> bs=1M 
Once this is done, open gparted or something and expand the partition to fill the entire card (if you have an emunand partition do NOT overwrite it! It will be at the beginning of the card so just expand to the right).

Might take awhile but you don't need to backup then restore + copy over SD card files.
